observation: Default semantic search exposed both conflicting memories with close similarity scores. Explicit lifecycle metadata filtering excluded the contested transient memory.
interpretation: Current Mem0 OSS preserves both conflicting memories, which is good for auditability. Semantic similarity alone does not express temporal/verification authority; the caller must encode lifecycle policy in retrieval filters or another verification layer.
limits: This uses infer=False to isolate memory storage and retrieval from LLM extraction.
Only one controlled conflict pair was executed live.
This does not claim Mem0 should automatically choose the verified fact; explicit filters are a supported mechanism.
The experiment validates an authority-policy boundary, not a global Mem0 quality ranking.
